html:
The first thing that happens when the couch leaves a Greer living room is that the floor tells the truth. Four pale rectangles of clean carpet where the legs sat, a gray line along the wall where the vacuum never reached, and a dozen small marks at hand height around the light switch. If you are doing a move out cleaning for a living room in Greer, that is the room to plan around, because it is large, it is the first thing a landlord or buyer walks into, and it has no cabinets to hide behind.

This guide covers the living room and the shared spaces around it: the entry, the hallway, the stairs, the dining nook and the coat closet. For kitchens and baths we have written separate pieces, including how we handle move-out bathrooms. Here the focus is the open, visible part of the house.

What the walkthrough looks at first

A lot of move-outs we see around Greer, from older homes near Downtown Greer and Trade Street to newer streets close to GSP Airport, share the same pattern. The kitchen gets the attention, and the living room gets a quick vacuum. Then the final inspection arrives and the notes say things like "marks on walls" and "dusty blinds," not "dirty oven."

When we walk through a home for the free estimate, we stand in the doorway of the living room and look at it the way an inspector would, in this order:

  1. The floor along the walls, where dust and pet hair pile up.
  2. Baseboards and the bottom of door frames.
  3. Light switches, outlet covers and the door handles people touch constantly.
  4. Window sills, the track the window slides in, and the blinds.
  5. Any closet that opens off the room.

Everything on that list is part of our move-out cleaning in Greer, so the estimate visit is mostly about condition, not about what is included.

Room by room: where the dirt hides in a living area

SpotWhat builds upHow we deal with it
Floor edges and cornersDust, hair, grit pressed into the carpet lineDetail the edges first, then vacuum or mop the open floor
BaseboardsDust on top, scuffs from furniture and vacuumsWiped by hand along their full length
Switches and handlesFingerprints, grime that looks like a shadowHand-wiped, including the plates and door frames
Window tracks and sillsDead insects, dirt, pollen in seasonVacuumed out, then wiped clean
BlindsDust on every slatWiped slat by slat

Notice how little of that list is about the middle of the room. That is on purpose. The middle of a living room cleans up in minutes. The edges take the time.

The shared spaces people forget

Entry and hallway

The front entry collects more than any other part of the house. Greer has plenty of red clay in the yards, and it comes inside on shoes. Even months after a family leaves, a faint orange tint can sit in the corner by the door and under the mat. We check the threshold, the door frame, and the first few feet of flooring closely.

Stairs and landings

If the home has stairs, the risers and the corner where each step meets the wall get the same treatment as the baseboards. Handrails get wiped too, since inspectors tend to put a hand on them.

The coat closet and the "mystery cabinet"

Shelves, rods and floors inside closets are on our list. A hall closet usually has a dusty shelf and a floor with a ring of grit. Built-in shelving beside a fireplace or media wall deserves the same check, because tenants often forget it exists until the last day.

What you can do before we arrive

  • Take everything off the floor, shelves and window sills. We clean around objects, but a bare room cleans faster and better.
  • Patch or note any wall damage so the cleaners do not scrub at something that is a repair, not dirt.
  • Take down curtains and rods, and fold up rugs you are keeping.
  • Leave the lights and water on until the cleaning is finished.
  • Mention pets. Hair along baseboards changes how we plan the first hour.

If you are still deciding between a regular clean and a full move-out, read about move-out cleaning in Taylors to see how the same checklist works a few minutes down the road, or look at our move-in and move-out cleaning service overview for the full list.

How much does move-out cleaning cost in Greer?

People searching "how much is move out cleaning" want a number, and we understand why. We do not give one over the phone, because the home decides it. Home size in rooms and square feet matters. So does the condition the last occupant left, whether the home is empty or still furnished, how much grease sits inside the oven and fridge, and how tight your closing or key-return date is. A small apartment left tidy and a four-bedroom with two dogs are not the same job.

That is why Perfect Services gives prices only after a free in-home estimate. It is a short visit to see the space with no commitment. Book it with the form on the Greer page, call (864) 399-5168 or text (864) 666-8520. If you are on a deadline, ask about the schedule when you book through our Greer move-out cleaning page, and we will tell you what is realistic.

How long does it take, and can I book this week?

A tidy, empty living area and entry are usually a small part of the day. The hours go into the kitchen, the bathrooms and the detail work on edges and tracks. Larger homes may need a team of more than one cleaner, which is how we handle a closing day with little room to spare. Availability changes week to week, so the fastest route is to request the estimate and mention your move date.

We are a Brazilian-owned team based right here in Greer, serving the 29650, 29651 and 29652 ZIP codes, and our method is detail first: edges, corners and frames get done by hand. If you want a dated plan for your move, request your free estimate or go straight to the Greer move-out booking form.
faqs: Do you clean walls in a living room during a move-out?

Our move-out checklist covers baseboards, doors, frames and light switches. If you have scuffs or marks on the walls, point them out at the estimate and we will tell you what can be cleaned and what is a paint job.
Should I leave the carpet cleaning for you too?
The move-out service vacuums and mops floors edge to edge. Deep carpet work is a separate question, so mention stains or odors at the free estimate and we will talk through your options.
How early should I book before my key-return date in Greer?
As early as you know the date. A free in-home estimate comes first, and tight closing or inspection days may need a larger team, so earlier notice gives us more room to fit you in.
